author: Unreal Engine
description:
Advanced simulation of non-visual spectrum sensors (IR, NVG) in Unreal Engine requires a specialized content pipeline that transforms standard visual assets into physically accurate representations across multiple electromagnetic spectrums beyond visible light. 

This recording of a session presented by Lockheed Martin at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 explores the technical framework for simulating these sensors through custom material properties, specialized render passes, and post-processing systems that accurately model phenomena like thermal signatures and night vision amplification characteristics. 

Lockheed Martin demonstrates how to extend Unreal Engine's rendering pipeline to support multi-spectral simulation while maintaining real-time performance, enabling high-fidelity training and testing environments for defense, aerospace, and autonomous systems applications.

Find out more about using Unreal Engine for simulation here: unrealengine.com/uses/simulation

#Simulation, #Lockhee
title: Advanced Simulation of Non-Visual Spectrum Sensors | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026

author: Unreal Engine
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026, Agora Studio explores how adopting Unreal Engine 5 has redefined the real-time animation pipeline behind their animated A-COM series. 

They take a deep dive into their streamlined creation process that begins with integrated previz, where instant playback of cameras, sets, and lighting help solidify the team’s initial intent and vision early. By rigging and animating directly in-engine with high-fidelity visuals, Agora Studio eliminates proxies and import/export loops, enabling artists to work continuously in full scene context. 

The talk showcases seamless editing with the Master Level Sequencer, complex rigging possibilities, and advanced animation workflows, including smears, stylization techniques, and shot sculpting.
